headlines.title: 1 dead, 1 arrested after solo-vehicle crash in southern Santa Clara County
headlines.description: One person died and another was arrested Saturday following a solo-vehicle crash in rural Santa Clara County. At about 6:30 p.m., California Highway Patrol officers were sent to the intersection of Monterey Road at Church Avenue in the unincorporated community of San Martin. When they got to the scene, officers found that a Ford SUV had veered off the road and hit a tree, killing the 31-year-old woman in the front passenger seat. Investigators believe that speed was a factor in the crash and arrested the driver on suspicion of vehicular manslaughter, CHP officials said in a news release Monday. The victim’s name wasn’t released, but the CHP said she was a resident of San Martin. Anyone with information about the crash can call the CHP Hollister-Gilroy Area office at (408) 427-0700.

headlines.title: Brentwood high school mourns 2 students killed in crash
headlines.description: Students at Brentwood’s Liberty High School on Monday were mourning two classmates killed in a crash over the weekend as the California Highway Patrol continued to investigate what led to the collision. Police responded just after midnight Sunday to the crash on Deer Valley Road near Balfour Road in Brentwood. Preliminary information indicates a BMW and an Infiniti sedan were involved in the collision. The Liberty High School students were in the Infiniti, according to authorities. Two students died at the scene. Another student and the driver of the BMW were taken to a hospital. Students who spoke with NBC Bay Area remembered their classmates as kind and funny. One student described one of the teens who died as a good, religious friend who had been helping him become a better Catholic. Another recalled one of the students who survived as a kind person whom she remembered for the pig he raised through FFA. “It’s truly, like, really sad to think about some kids got their lives taken so young, when they were just about to start their life and be outside of high school,” Liberty High School student Hannah Jorstad said. “And I think that it truly affects us because it really shows us how fast our lives can go and how we really need to appreciate the people around us and be kind to the people around us.” Liberty High School said counseling services would be available Monday for students dealing with grief following the crash. “With deep sadness, we share that two Liberty High School students passed away and another student was injured in a tragic car accident Saturday night,” Principal Efa Huckaby said in a message to the school community. “Our hearts are with their families, friends, classmates, teammates, and everyone affected by this tragedy. This loss will be felt throughout our school community,” Huckaby said. There were reports that the BMW may have been involved in a police pursuit around the time of the crash, but CHP said there was no active pursuit. Antioch police said the BMW was instead wanted in connection with a pursuit involving a different law enforcement agency days earlier. CHP is investigating the cause of the crash. Contra Costa County Sep 13 Contra Costa County 22 hours ago 2 dead, 2 injured in late-night two-vehicle crash in rural Brentwood

headlines.title: Crews start to remove trees from San Francisco waterfront park
headlines.description: Crews on Monday started the process of removing nearly 100 trees from San Francisco’s waterfront as part of the Embarcadero Plaza and Sue Bierman Park renovation project. The tree removal work is expected to take up to five weeks, according to San Francisco Recreation and Parks. Park visitors should expect intermittent sidewalk closures, construction noise, and detours, but impacts on parking and traffic should be minimal. A total of 97 of the park’s 113 trees will come down. Three will be transplanted to new locations within the park. The others will be replaced with a mix of species, including coast live oak, coast redwood, Monterey cypress and more, according to the recreation and parks department. Visit the San Francisco Recreation and Parks website to learn more.

headlines.title: New warnings about the risks of AI to humanity revive a long-running debate
headlines.description: New warnings from within the artificial intelligence industry have revived a long-running debate over whether advanced AI could escape human control and ultimately threaten humanity’s survival, and whether the companies developing the technology are doing enough to prevent such a scenario. The CEO of Anthropic, the San Francisco company behind Claude, said he thought the industry needed to reduce the speed of its work, cautioning Saturday that a swarm of AI agents might be able to take over the internet in six months to a year unless companies devoted more time to putting safeguards in place. Days after two former Anthropic safety researchers publicly aired concerns that the existential threats AI might poste to humanity were receiving too little attention, Dario Amodei outlined a plan for companies like his and governments around the world to ensure that increasingly capable AI models remain aligned with the commands and values of responsible people. Sam Altman, CEO of ChatGPT maker OpenAI, said this weekend that companies should start coordinating on AI safety without waiting for the government to introduce legislation. The “pacing” of AI development doesn’t mean stopping it, Altman wrote on X. “But it should be slower than it otherwise could be.” Here’s what to know about the recent dire predictions and whether any brakes might be put on AI advancement: AI models are becoming more powerful Concerns over the potential risks of the technology are rising as new AI models become more powerful, heightening both the potential for misuse by people with criminal aims, such as creating and spreading a disease that kills most of the world’s population, and the risk of AI systems going rogue in a dangerous way. Anthropic disclosed last week that it blocked efforts by bad actors to use its AI models for malicious activity, such as cyberattacks, surveillance and research that could have led to biological weapons. The company said it put stronger safeguards in its latest models to restrict biological research that could be used to make weapons but noted that “as models become increasingly capable, their risks will increase, unless AI developers and society’s defenders act to make them safer.” Last year, Anthropic reported that hackers used the company’s AI in a cyberattack targeting about 30 companies and government agencies around the world. It said the hackers were very likely part of a Chinese state-sponsored group. Multiple AI models have acted on their own When an AI agent “goes rogue,” it means the AI has taken action beyond the task it was asked to perform. Both Anthropic and OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, said in July that their AI models had acted on their own. Anthropic disclosed that three AI models — Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Mythos 5 and an internal research test model — hacked into three other organizations during testing, just days after OpenAI revealed that its AI system hacked into the servers of AI startup Hugging Face. OpenAI described the intrusion by a combination of models, including its newly released GPT‑5.6 Sol and an “even more capable” model that was still being tested internally, as a “significant security incident.” Meta followed suit in early August with a similar case of an AI model finding ways around another company’s digital security. Although some observers noted that people had disabled some guardrails in the OpenAI and Anthropic cases, the episodes seemed to reflect one of the biggest fears around AI: that if models achieve artificial general intelligence, or AGI, a loosely defined term for AI that can match or surpass human abilities across a broad range of intellectual tasks, the technology could cause an irreversible catastrophic event or subjugate the human race. How or when AI might cause a catastrophe is debated Doomsday scenarios generally fall into two categories: An AI that achieves self-improving superintelligence and controls people instead of vice versa, or AI used by a rogue state or nefarious actors. Worries that artificial intelligence might overcome human limits on its reach or actions are not new. Alan Turing, a British mathematician widely regarded as one of the earliest authorities on artificial intelligence, predicted in 1951 that AI would eventually take control from humans. Less than a decade later, Norbert Wiener, another mathematician, warned intelligent machines would seek to accomplish their own objectives and humans would not be able to stop them. In 2026, how reasonable are fears that AI, either by escaping human control or through misuse by unscrupulous people, could cause a cataclysmic event or the downfall of civilization? No one knows. Experts across computer science, philosophy and other fields have envisioned numerous routes by which a future AI system might cause a global catastrophe, either by escaping human control or in the hands of an unscrupulous people. They range from deploying weapons and identifying a lethal pathogen to manipulating governments into conflict or disrupting the food, energy and communications networks societies rely on to function. There is no widely accepted estimate for how soon any of these scenarios might happen and no consensus on their likelihood. In 2023, the nonprofit Center for AI Safety issued a statement cosigned by more than 350 researchers and technology executives, including Anthropic’s Amodei and OpenAI’s Altman, saying: “Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside pandemics and nuclear war.” The 2026 International AI Safety Report, written with guidance from more than 100 independent experts, says current systems show early signs of some relevant capabilities but not at levels that could enable a loss of control, and describes the risk’s likelihood, nature and timing as “unusually ambiguous.” Some are stressing the need for AI safeguards before it’s too late An Anthropic researcher said last week he was resigning from the company over concerns that neither the company nor its competitors were acting responsibly in developing the technology. In social media posts, Jacob Coxon estimated a 10% chance of AI causing human extinction within the next decade and said both Anthropic and OpenAI “are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.” Researchers have called for a slowdown of AI development and warned for years that the technology could pose existential risks to humanity. Following the recent incidents, experts called for improved testing by AI companies and more dialogue between the U.S. and China to come up with shared solutions. But AI is growing so fast that government and evaluation systems are struggling to keep pace with the technology. Countries are cobbling together their own laws, some conflicting. Chinese leader Xi Jinping warned at a conference in July of the need to keep AI from evading human control. The Trump administration initially demonstrated reluctance to regulate AI but has become more keen to reduce cybersecurity risks. On Sunday, President Donald Trump downplayed the necessity for his administration to check AI development, but acknowledged the need for some regulation. __ AP Business Writer Kelvin Chan contributed from London

headlines.title: 7 people injured after multi-vehicle crash in San Francisco
headlines.description: At about 6 a.m., San Francisco police and fire crews responded to the intersection of Bayshore Boulevard and Industrial Street. When they arrived on the scene, emergency crews found that a four-vehicle collision injured seven people, five of whom were taken to the hospital for treatment, according to San Francisco Fire Department spokesperson Samuel Menchaca. All of the injured people are expected to recover, according to police officials. The cause of the crash wasn’t disclosed but police said drugs and alcohol don’t appear to have been a factor.

headlines.title: 3.0 magnitude earthquake shakes Contra Costa County
headlines.description: A preliminary 3.0 magnitude earthquake struck near Brentwood Monday morning, according to the United States Geological Survey. The quake was centered 6.5 miles northeast of Blackhawk and 7.4 miles west-southwest of Brentwood, the USGS said. This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates. headlines.title: Gilroy to vote on pausing new data center development
headlines.description: The Gilroy City Council is expected to vote Monday night on whether to temporarily ban the development of new data centers across the city. Data centers house computer systems used to power artificial intelligence and other technology. The facilities can be large and noisy for nearby residents and use significant amounts of electricity and water for cooling, putting additional strain on power and water systems. If approved, the temporary citywide moratorium would halt new data center development applications. The pause would allow the city to review and update its regulations for future data centers and other large industrial projects. The decision would not affect the controversial $2 billion Amazon data center already under construction in Gilroy. “Community members have raised important questions and concerns about how Gilroy should evaluate projects of this size and intensity in the future, and we are taking that feedback seriously,” Gilroy Mayor Greg Bozzo said in a statement. Bozzo said a temporary pause would give the city an opportunity to examine its existing standards, determine where they could be strengthened and bring proposed changes back to the community for public discussion. The discussion comes as another Bay Area city considers similar restrictions. The Hayward City Council is expected to discuss a potential ban on new data center development Tuesday following significant public opposition from residents.

headlines.title: 4 hospitalized after head-on crash in Contra Costa County
headlines.description: A head-on crash in Contra Costa County caused traffic to back up for miles Monday morning and sent four people to the hospital. The crash happened at about 7:45 a.m. near Marsh Creek Road and Morgan Territory Road. Police said a truck traveling eastbound crossed the double yellow lines and crashed head-on into a Kia. The truck driver, the driver of the Kia and two children inside the Kia were taken to the hospital. No major injuries were reported. Investigators said drugs and alcohol were not involved in the crash. Lanes reopened at about 8:30 a.m., though traffic remained backed up for some time afterward. The cause of the crash remains under investigation.

headlines.title: California sues Trump administration over immigration rule change
headlines.description: California filed a lawsuit Monday challenging the Trump administration’s new public charge rule, marking the state’s 92nd legal action against the administration. California Attorney General Rob Bonta announced the lawsuit in San Francisco alongside San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu and Santa Clara County Counsel Tony LoPresti. Bonta said it is the second time California has sued the Trump administration over its public charge policy. According to Bonta and other officials, the new rule gives immigration officers discretion to deny a green card based on an applicant’s use of public benefit programs. NBC Bay Area’s Ginger Conejero Saab has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: 2 pedestrians seriously hurt in separate hit and runs in Antioch
headlines.description: Two pedestrians were seriously injured in separate hit-and-run crashes over the weekend in Antioch, with both victims airlifted to trauma centers, police said. The first crash happened around 6:50 p.m. Saturday near East 18th Street and Phillips Lane. Officers found a 54-year-old man with severe leg injuries. The man was later flown to a trauma center. The driver fled the scene, and witnesses described the vehicle as a dark gray sedan, police said. That same night, a separate crash was reported just before 10 p.m. at 801 Sunset Dr. Officers arrived three minutes later and found a 63-year-old woman with major injuries to her arms and legs. The woman was also airlifted to a trauma center. The vehicle involved had already fled when officers arrived, police said. Anyone who witnessed either crash, has surveillance or dashcam footage from the areas around the time of these case, or has information about the fleeing vehicles is urged to contact Sgt. Green with the Traffic Unit at 925-779-6864. Anonymous tips can be submitted.

headlines.title: San Francisco's OpenAI won't go public amid fears about AI safety and security
headlines.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says the San Francisco company will not go public this year amid heightened fears about artificial intelligence safety and security. It was all spurred by a viral social media post from Jacob Coxon, a former employee at leading AI firm Anthropic, who warned that the rapid development of AI could lead to the extinction of humankind by the end of the decade. In an interview with “Meet The Press” Sunday, Coxon reiterated his concerns. “You’re building a human level or super human level mind without understanding what it wants or thinks or the way it thinks, and I think that intrinsically should be quite scary,” he said. In an interview with Fortune Magazine on Saturday, Altman said the San Francisco AI giant will not go public this year. “We understand the magnitude of the responsibility on us,” he said. “We understand what could go wrong. There are decisions we should not be able to make, there are risks we should not be able to incur on behalf of humanity.” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei wrote in a new essay, “We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models.” However, President Donald Trump expressed concerns about an AI slowdown. “We’re leading China in AI, we’re the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins,” he said. “We can put guardrails. We can do this and that.” Last week, former President Barrack Obama said AI could be dangerous if more isn’t done and urged Democrats to prioritize AI controls.

headlines.title: Person rescued after falling off cliff near Panther Beach in Santa Cruz County
headlines.description: A person was rescued after falling off a cliff near Panther Beach in Santa Cruz County on Sunday, Cal Fire CZU said. Cal Fire CZU said on Sunday afternoon a person fell between 25-30 feet off a cliff south of Panther Beach, landing on a rock shelf. Authorities said responders packaged the person before Cal Fire BEU Copter 610 out of Hollister Air Attack Base hoisted the patient to the bluffs, where a Stanford Life Flight was waiting to take them to the hospital. Cal Fire CZU said the person was in stable condition.
